items.name: Algorithm
items.doc: Web Crypto algorithm parameters, one struct for all of them (fields as the spec names them): { name: "AES-GCM", iv }, { name: "HMAC", hash: "SHA-256" }, { name: "ECDSA", hash: "SHA-256" }, { name: "ECDSA", namedCurve: "P-256" }, { name: "ECDH", public: key }, { name: "HKDF", hash, salt, info }, { name: "PBKDF2", hash, salt, iterations }, { name: "AES-GCM", length: 256 }.

members.name: name
members.doc: The algorithm's name ("AES-GCM", "HMAC", "ECDSA", "ECDH", "HKDF", "PBKDF2"; any case), or, for digest, the hash's.

members.name: hash
members.doc: The hash ("SHA-256", …) for HMAC, ECDSA, HKDF and PBKDF2. HMAC falls back on the key's.

members.name: namedCurve
members.doc: The curve for generateKey and importKey of ECDSA ("P-256", "P-384") and ECDH keys (also "X25519").

members.name: length
members.doc: The key length in bits for generateKey (AES-GCM: 128, 192 or 256; HMAC: 256 unless given).

members.name: iv
members.doc: AES-GCM's nonce (required; 12 bytes is usual).

members.name: additionalData
members.doc: AES-GCM's authenticated, unencrypted data (none unless given).

members.name: tagLength
members.doc: AES-GCM's tag length in bits: only 128 (the default) is supported.

members.name: public
members.doc: ECDH's peer public key, for deriveBits.

members.name: salt
members.doc: The HKDF or PBKDF2 salt (empty unless given).

members.name: info
members.doc: HKDF's context info (empty unless given).

members.name: iterations
members.doc: PBKDF2's iteration count.

items.name: Arena
items.doc: Explicitly managed memory for unsafe code (spec §9.4): alloc hands out zeroed storage for plain data (no references), which the collector doesn't trace and which stays valid until free(). Pointers into it dangle afterwards (undefined behavior). The scoped arena { … } block needs none of this.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: An arena that reserves memory in chunks of capacity bytes (4096 if it isn't positive; a bigger allocation gets a chunk of its own).

members.name: alloc
members.doc: Room for count zeroed Ts (plain data: no references), as a pointer to the first.

members.name: free
members.doc: Frees everything allocated from this arena.

items.name: AsyncIterator
items.signature: class AsyncIterator<T, E extends Error = never>
items.doc: An async iterator (spec §5.7): next() promises the next value, or null once done (so, like Iterator, a T that is itself nullable can't be told apart from the end). async function* g(): AsyncIterator<T> throws E makes one: its step function yields suspensions, both for await and, after storing the value, for yield v.

members.doc: An iterator with no steps (an async function* makes the ones that produce values).

members.name: next
members.doc: Promises the next value, or null once done. The promise rejects with what the generator throws (and later calls give null). Calls made before earlier ones are fulfilled queue up, in order.

members.doc: for await uses the iterator itself.

items.name: Conn
items.doc: A TCP connection: chunks of bytes with read or for await, the rest as text with text(), writes (in the order they're made) with write/writeText. One read at a time.

members.doc: This side's address.

members.name: remoteAddr

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(fd: int, localAddr: Addr, remoteAddr: Addr)
members.doc: A connection on descriptor fd; made by connect and accept, not by programs.

members.name: readable
members.doc: The connection's incoming bytes as a stream (reading it and read() don't mix).

members.name: writable
members.doc: The connection's outgoing bytes as a stream: closing it finishes writing (closeWrite()), aborting it closes the connection.

members.name: read
members.doc: Up to n bytes (as soon as some arrive), or null once the other side has finished writing (or this side is closed).

members.name: next
members.doc: for await reads chunks until the end.

members.name: asyncIterator
members.doc: The connection itself (for await (const chunk of conn)).

members.name: text
members.doc: Everything until the other side finishes writing, as text (UTF-8; anything else rejects with kind "InvalidData").

members.name: write
members.doc: Writes all of data; the count written.

members.name: writeText
members.doc: Writes text as UTF-8; the count of bytes written.

members.name: closeWrite
members.doc: Finishes writing once earlier writes are done (the other side reads the end); reading goes on.

members.name: close
members.doc: Closes the connection once earlier writes are done: a waiting read ends with null. Twice is fine.

modules.name: std/os
modules.about:
std/os (spec §13.4): where things go on this system: the home directory, the temporary directory, and the per-user directories for an application's data, caches and configuration.

           Linux (XDG)                       macOS                           Windows

data $XDG_DATA_HOME, ~/.local/share ~/Library/Application Support %APPDATA% localData as data as data %LOCALAPPDATA% cache $XDG_CACHE_HOME, ~/.cache ~/Library/Caches %LOCALAPPDATA% config $XDG_CONFIG_HOME, ~/.config ~/Library/Application Support %APPDATA% state $XDG_STATE_HOME, ~/.local/state — —

They come from the environment (a variable that is empty or not an absolute path is ignored, as the XDG specification says), so they can be null when nothing says. Nothing is created: an application makes its own directory below one of them.

The Windows functions follow Node's path.win32: \ and / both separate, drive letters (C:) and UNC roots (\\server\share), results use \; comparisons in relative ignore case. Not yet: the per-drive working directories (resolve("D:x") uses D:\), \\?\ paths, toNamespacedPath.

modules.name: std/posix
modules.about:
std/posix (spec §12.3; Linux and macOS): the POSIX calls packages that talk to devices need, declared once. C header imports leave out variadic functions (open, fcntl, ioctl) and macros that glibc builds from others (O_CLOEXEC), so packages used to declare their own; two declarations of one C symbol with different signatures don't link, so they must come from here. The others have c:unistd.h's parameters (a buffer is ptr<u8>, which is void * to the linker), so a program can use both. Buffers go to C as ptr.bytes(view) inside unsafe.

import { open, close, ioctl, errno, errnoMessage, O_RDWR, O_CLOEXEC } from "std/posix"
const fd = open("/dev/ttyUSB0", (O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC) as c_int)
if (fd < 0) throw new Error(errnoMessage())

items.name: errno
items.doc: errno: why the last failed call failed (read it right after the call).

items.name: errnoMessage
items.doc: The system's text for error number e (strerror), by default the last one.

Reading or writing a pipe and waiting for a child are jobs on runtime threads that settle on the event loop.

modules.name: std/test
modules.about:
std/test (spec §14.3): a Vitest-like test API. describe/test register tests while the file's top level runs; they run (in order) once it's done, and the file reports each one and a summary, exiting with 1 when any failed. pico test runs every *.test.pi file in parallel, one process each; pico run x.test.pi runs one.

A failed expectation stops a test (it panics, and the runner catches that); after an await it's recorded and the test goes on. A panic or an exception in a test fails it. Async tests are async functions or async lambdas (it("…", async () => { … })). Environment: PICO_TEST_FILTER (only tests whose full name contains it), PICO_TEST_MODE=bench (run the benchmarks instead), PICO_TEST_TIMES=0 (no durations, for reproducible output).

modules.name: std/text
modules.about: std/text (spec §13.11, decision 344): edit distance, for "did you mean …?" suggestions, and converting names between camelCase, kebab-case and snake_case.

items.name: editDistance
items.signature: function editDistance(a: string, b: string): int
items.doc: The edit distance between a and b: the fewest insertions, deletions, substitutions and swaps of two neighbouring characters that turn one into the other (Damerau-Levenshtein, as optimal string alignment: no substring is edited twice). Characters are code points.

items.name: camelCase
items.signature: function camelCase(s: string, separators: string = "-_ "): string
items.doc: s in camel case: the words between separators (by default -, _ and spaces) joined, each after the first starting with an upper-case letter; letters are otherwise kept as they are. camelCase("pizza-type") is "pizzaType", camelCase("max_retry count") "maxRetryCount".

items.name: kebabCase
items.doc: s in kebab case: its words in lower case, joined with -. Words are separated by -, _ and whitespace, and where a lower-case letter or a digit meets an upper-case one (fooBar) or an upper-case run ends (HTTPServer). kebabCase("pizzaType") is "pizza-type".

items.name: snakeCase
items.doc: s in snake case: its words (as kebabCase finds them) in lower case, joined with _. snakeCase("maxRetryCount") is "max_retry_count".

modules.name: std/timers
modules.about:
std/timers: promise-based timers (spec §10.5) that can be cancelled with a signal.

import { delay } from "std/timers", then await delay(100, ac.signal).

items.name: delay
items.signature: function delay(ms: int, signal: AbortSignal? = null): Promise<void, AbortError>
items.doc: Settles after ms milliseconds; rejects with AbortError as soon as signal is aborted (right away if it already is), and the timer is cleared.

items.name: TimeoutError
items.doc: What withTimeout rejects with when the time runs out.

members.name: ms
members.doc: The time that ran out, in milliseconds.

items.name: withTimeout
items.signature: function withTimeout<T, E extends Error>(promise: Promise<T, E>, ms: int): Promise<T, Error>
items.doc: promise's value or error if it settles within ms milliseconds, else a TimeoutError. The work isn't stopped, only no longer waited for (give it an AbortSignal to stop it); a failure it has later is ignored.

modules.name: std/worker
modules.about:
std/worker (spec §10.2): the worker side of a worker thread.

import { self } from "std/worker", then self.onmessage = (job: Job) => { … } and self.postMessage(result).

items.name: WorkerSelf
items.doc: The worker's side of its channel to the parent: self is the one instance.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A handle on the current worker's channel; use self rather than making another.

members.name: postMessage
members.signature: public postMessage<T extends Sendable>(message: T, options: TransferOptions? = null): void
members.doc: Sends a copy of message to the parent (nothing in the main thread); options.transfer: buffers moved instead.

members.name: close
members.doc: Stops listening: the worker ends once nothing else is pending.

items.name: self
items.doc: This worker (set onmessage on it to receive the parent's messages).

items.name: parallelMap
items.signature: function parallelMap<T extends Sendable, U extends Sendable, E extends Error>( items: T[], f: (item: T) => U throws E, workers: int, ): Promise<U[], E>
items.doc: f over every item, in parallel on up to workers inline workers (spec §10.4); the results in order. f must not capture anything.

items.name: WorkerPool
items.signature: class WorkerPool<In extends Sendable, Out extends Sendable>
items.doc: A fixed number of workers running the same module (new WorkerPool<In, Out>("./job", size: n)); run(job) sends a job to the least busy one and promises its next message.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: (module is the module's id: the compiler rewrites the path.)

members.name: size
members.doc: The number of workers (size, at least 1).

members.name: run
members.doc: Sends job to the worker with the fewest jobs waiting. Rejects with a WorkerPanicked if that worker dies or the pool is terminated first.

members.name: terminate
members.doc: Stops every worker; jobs still waiting for an answer reject with a WorkerPanicked.
